# xoveconsulting-com-tests

A Playwright + JUnit 5 test framework for https://xoveconsulting.com, generated by
[Suite Builder](https://github.com/ghost-in-the-kernel/suite-builder) from a crawl of the site.

## Run it

Needs Java 17+ and Maven. From this folder:

```
mvn test -Dgroups=smoke                every page type loads (start here)
mvn test                               all tests, headless
mvn test -Dgroups=navigation           header, footer and page links land on the right pages
mvn test -Dgroups=menus                links inside dropdown menus
mvn test -Dheaded=true                 watch it in a browser (half a second per action; -DslowMo=1000)
mvn test -Dbrowser=firefox             in Firefox, or -Dbrowser=webkit (Safari's engine); Chromium by default
mvn test -Dgroups=harness              the harness testing itself (HarnessTest; runs with every group anyway)
mvn test -DbaseUrl=https://staging.example.com   against another copy of the site
mvn test -DblockAds=false              with ads (blocked by default: they hijack clicks; for every
                                       run, <blockAds>false</blockAds> in pom.xml's YOURS properties)
mvn test -Dtrace=always                keep every test's trace (target/traces/), not only failures'
```

Each test prints a line as it starts (`-> SmokeTest: ...`) and how long it took. A test that
fails leaves its evidence in `target/failures/<TestClass>/<test>/`: a screenshot, the page's HTML,
its steps, console errors, failed requests and a Playwright trace (open it at
https://trace.playwright.dev). Each run starts clean: the last run's failures move to
`target/failures-previous/`, so rerunning one test keeps the rest of a full run's evidence one
run back. `SuiteRulesTest` runs with every group and reports each of the suite's rules
(`SUITE-RULES.md`: how tests are written, and that no generated file is edited outside its
YOURS blocks); a broken rule says where, why the rule exists, and what to change, and no test runs
until it is fixed. A page gets 30
seconds to load and a check 10 seconds; no test runs longer than 2 minutes.

The first run downloads Playwright's browsers (a minute or so). Before a demo, do that once ahead
of time:

```
mvn exec:java -e -Dexec.mainClass=com.microsoft.playwright.CLI -Dexec.args="install chromium"
```

Each page object's `open()` accepts the cookie banner once per test, with its own time limit, and
prints what happened; a banner it can't accept never fails a test by itself (see
`core/CookieBanner`).

## What's here

```
com/xoveconsulting/tests/
  core/       LoadablePage (get(), load(), isLoaded()), WaitActions, CookieBanner, SiteConfig
  core/actions/  ClickableAction, CheckableAction, EnterableAction, ClearableAction,
                 ReadableAction, VerifiableAction, ExecutableTask
  uri/        UrlPaths: every page's path
  pages/header/  HeaderElements, FooterElements: the 12 links on nearly every page, and
                 actions/HeaderNavigableActions: every page's navigateTo()
  pages/      one package per page type, e.g. home/:
    HomePage       open(), isLoaded(): URL, full page load, title, key elements
    HomeElements   locators: section headings, links, a marked place for your own
    HomeTasks      multi-step tasks
    actions/       HomeClickActions, HomeCheckActions, HomeEnterActions, HomeClearActions,
                   HomeReadActions, HomeVerifyActions
```

Page types found (6):

| Class | Kind | URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HomePage` | one-off | `/` |
| `SiteDetailPage` | family, ~3 pages | `/*` |
| `SiteDetailPage2` | family, ~2 pages | `/*` |
| `SiteDetailPage3` | family, ~3 pages | `/*` |
| `SiteDetailPage4` | family, ~2 pages | `/*` |
| `CareersPage` | one-off | `/careers.php` |

Tests read like this:

```java
new HomePage(page).open().navigateTo().xoveConsultingServices();
```

## Adding elements

Each `<Type>Elements` enum has a marked place for the page's own elements. The section headings
it starts with are the ones every crawled page of that type showed; keep what matters.
Locators from [Selector Grabber](https://github.com/ghost-in-the-kernel/selector-grabber) paste
straight in:

```java
SUBMIT_BUTTON(page -> page.locator("xpath=//button[@data-testid='submit']")),
```

Then use them from the Click and Verify actions, and write the tests that need thinking in the
`stories` package.

## Editing, and regenerating

Every file says in its first lines what may be edited. Most are generated with **YOURS** blocks:

```java
    // ==== YOURS (elements): safe to edit; regenerating keeps what is between these lines ====
    SUBMIT_BUTTON(page -> page.locator("xpath=//button[@data-testid='submit']")),
    // ==== END YOURS (elements) ====
```

Regenerating (a new crawl of a changed site) rewrites everything else and keeps what is in the
blocks. Work that no longer has a place (its page type was renamed, say) is moved to
`orphaned/`, never deleted. Files that are wholly yours (`CHANGES.md`, your
story tests) are never touched.

## Working with an AI

`AI-README.md` is written for an AI assistant: hand it this folder (zipped is fine), a user story
and the pages the story touches, saved from the browser into `saved-pages/`, and ask for the test.
The crawl this was generated from is in `crawl/`: keep it with the project, and zip the whole
folder when you hand it on.
